_coverage.title: add_to_waitlist: when nothing open works for the patient, offer the waitlist; add them only if they agree.

name: offer_waitlist_when_no_times_fit_without_adding
input: I really need something after 3pm next week. Do you have anything then?

conversation.content: Hi, I need to book a follow-up sometime next week.
Sure, I can help with that. Can you share your full name and date of birth so I can find your chart?
Thanks, one moment while I check what we have next week for a follow-up.
I have some openings next week for a follow-up: Tuesday at 9:20am, Wednesday at 10:40am, or Friday at 8:40am at Elm Street. Do any of those work?
No, I can’t do mornings at all. I really need something after 3pm next week. Do you have anything then?

grading_criteria:
The assistant must:
- Understand from find_open_slots that there are no appointments after 3pm next week, so nothing currently open meets the patient’s constraint.
- Clearly tell the patient there is nothing available after 3pm next week.
- Proactively offer the waitlist as an option (e.g., asking if they’d like to be added for earlier openings that fit their preferences).
- Not call add_to_waitlist in this turn, because the patient did not yet agree to be added.
- Keep the tone short, friendly, and consistent with the texting style rules.

checks.states_no_matching_times: Does the assistant explicitly say that there are no open appointments after 3pm next week that meet the patient’s request?
checks.offers_waitlist_option: Does the assistant offer being added to the waitlist as an option once it knows nothing open works?
checks.no_waitlist_without_consent: Does the assistant avoid calling add_to_waitlist before the patient has clearly agreed to be added?
